hints.junior: A budget in a doc only works if someone remembers to check it, every single time, forever. That's not a plan, that's hoping.
hints.mid: The failure mode here is a slow leak, not one bad PR. Every individual change looks fine in review.
hints.staff: Zero cost to violate plus zero signal when it happens converges to 'the biggest size nobody complained about yet,' not the agreed number.

hints.junior: Same starting number, two very different results, depending on whether anything actually checks it on every change.
hints.mid: The CI-gated version fails at the exact PR that crossed the line, with the size delta right there.
hints.staff: The tool existing in a doc nobody's CI reads is functionally the same as the tool not existing.

hints.junior: size-limit measures your real build output and fails the PR if it's over the number you set. No remembering required.
hints.mid: The config lives in the repo, reviewed like any other code, not in a wiki page someone has to go check by hand.
hints.staff: This turns a social problem, remembering or challenging a PR on size, into a mechanical one: the check is red or it isn't.

hints.junior: Treat a crossed budget like a failing test: fix the size, or make a deliberate, visible decision to raise the number.
hints.mid: Track every meaningful entry point, not just main.js, a lazy-loaded route can regress invisibly if only the main bundle is watched.
hints.staff: Measure gzip or brotli size, not raw bytes, that's what actually crosses the network and what your budget should reflect.

sections.junior: Hey! Today's case is about a bundle-size budget that only lived in a doc, and grew from 180 kilobytes to 340 kilobytes without a single PR looking like the one that broke it.
The fix is making the budget a real CI check, using something like size-limit, so it fails the pull request the moment your build goes over.
Compare a budget that only exists in a wiki page against one wired into CI, and see which one actually catches the regression.
A documented budget is a wish. A CI-enforced budget is a gate. Only one of them actually holds.
